correctness.rationale: The geometric fixed-point criterion requires the full edge support to be a union of edge orbits. For prime p each nontrivial step-edge orbit is a Hamiltonian p-cycle, ensuring 2-connectivity; for composite n the {0,a} edge orbit under r^a is restricted to a proper coset and disconnected; for prime k≥3 a full Hamiltonian cycle is invariant yet not 3-connected. The cited Babson–Björner–Linusson–Shareshian–Welker Theorem 3.1 says K_{p,2} ≃ wedge^(p−2)! S^(2p−5), so p≥5 gives a simply connected, (d−1)-connected free C_p-cover. The integral Serre/Cartan–Leray spectral sequence has only rows t=0 and t=d; differentials cannot alter base classes in total degrees <d. The classifying pullback is a multiplicative graded-ring isomorphism there; H*(BC_p;Z)=Z[eta]/(p eta), |eta|=2, yields nonzero u^j for 1≤j≤p−3. The homology statement and fundamental group follow likewise. The result does not claim higher-degree ring or exact category. A fresh complete p=5 enumeration confirms 785 non-two-connected nonempty faces and 157 free cyclic cell orbits, but is only finite corroboration.

final_claim: For n≥3 and 1≤k<n, free regular C_n action on the non-k-connected spanning-graph simplicial complex occurs precisely for prime n and k=1,2. For every prime p≥5 the ordinary C_p quotient at k=2 has classifying-pulled-back integral cohomology ring H*(BC_p;Z) in degrees <2p−5, hence u^(p−3) ≠0 and normalized category at least p−3.
